s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic abdominal discomfort with worsening diarrhea and generalized weakness
salient_findings: Green-brown slimy stools multiple times per day
Diffuse colonic wall thickening with pericolonic stranding on abdominal CT
Intensely fludeoxyglucose-avid focus in the left anterior pelvis on PET scan
key_facts: 92-year-old woman with hyperlipidemia and pulmonary sarcoidosis
Previously treated with steroids
Internal hemorrhoids
1-week history of worsening diarrhea and abdominal discomfort
Poor appetite and generalized weakness
Last colonoscopy at age 80 was unremarkable
Hospitalized for rectal bleeding 9 months earlier
Abdominal CT showed left-sided colitis and possible diverticulitis
PET scan showed intensely fludeoxyglucose-avid focus in the left anterior pelvis
Temperature 98.8°F, heart rate 80 bpm, and blood pressure 102/70 mm Hg on admission
White blood cell count 9.8 K/μL, hemoglobin 12 g/dL, and C-reactive protein 27.0 mg/dL
Fecal calprotectin 2562.8 μg/g and carcinoembryonic antigen 1.7
Stool tests for bacterial culture, PCR, Clostridioides difficile, ova and parasites, and leukocytes were negative

shortlist.label: Colorectal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Intensely fludeoxyglucose-avid focus in the left anterior pelvis on PET scan, suggestive of malignancy

shortlist.label: Ulcerative colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse colonic wall thickening with pericolonic stranding on abdominal CT, suggesting extensive inflammation

shortlist.label: Diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Previous abdominal CT showing left-sided colitis and possible diverticulitis

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Worsening diarrhea, abdominal discomfort, and elevated fecal calprotectin, consistent with inflammatory bowel disease

shortlist.label: Ischemic colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal CT showing diffuse colonic wall thickening, which could be indicative of ischemic changes

raw.rationale: The patient's history of rectal bleeding, abdominal CT showing left-sided colitis and a mass in the ascending colon, PET scan showing an intensely fludeoxyglucose-avid focus in the left anterior pelvis, and elevated carcinoembryonic antigen level are all suggestive of colorectal cancer.

rejected.label: Ulcerative colitis
rejected.why: While the patient has colitis, the presence of a mass and the PET scan findings are more suggestive of cancer.

rejected.label: Diverticulitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are not typical for diverticulitis, and the presence of a mass is not consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of prior history of inflammatory bowel disease make this diagnosis less likely, and the imaging findings are more suggestive of cancer.

rejected.label: Ischemic colitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are not typical for ischemic colitis, and the presence of a mass is not consistent with this diagnosis.
